s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive headaches and visual field defect with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage and a left occipital mass
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Noncontrast head CT showed left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage
Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields
Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive headaches and visual field defect with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage and a left occipital mass
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI

Normal vital signs

Noncontrast head CT showed left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and high mitotic rate, consistent with angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Meningeal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, and histopathological examination demonstrated features consistent with meningeal sarcoma

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed an extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage, and histopathological examination demonstrated branching ectatic vasculature, consistent with hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Gliosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Biphasic pattern of glial and mesenchymal differentiation was considered, although not definitively diagnosed

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD99, which can be seen in solitary fibrous tumors, although other features are not as typical

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination showing spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and the immunohistochemical studies with strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 are consistent with Hemangiopericytoma, a vascular tumor that can present with hemorrhage and has a characteristic staining pattern.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While angiosarcoma could explain the vascular features, the specific immunohistochemical profile and histopathological characteristics are more suggestive of Hemangiopericytoma.

rejected.label: Meningeal sarcoma
rejected.why: Meningeal sarcoma is a broader category and the specific features described are more typical of Hemangiopericytoma.

rejected.label: Gliosarcoma
rejected.why: Gliosarcoma typically shows a biphasic pattern of glial and mesenchymal differentiation, which is not the primary description provided.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Solitary fibrous tumors can express CD99 but typically have a more uniform appearance and lack the prominent vascular features described.
